title: Using the Zero Trust Mode Menu in Native Browser Experience

blocks.text: In Native Browser Experience Mode for Zero Trust Browser, users can opt for a typical browser view while still benefiting from the protection of an isolated session.

All capabilities of an isolated session are included when using Native Browser Experience Mode, and are accessible via the Zero Trust Mode menu. The default setting for Native Browser Experience Mode hides the menu from view.
When in the mobile isolation user experience, some of these capabilities are different or limited. To learn more, see Mobile User Experience in Isolation and Ranges & Limitations.

blocks.heading: Accessing the Zero Trust Mode Menu

blocks.text: To access the Zero Trust Mode menu:

blocks.item: Begin an isolated session in Native Browser Experience Mode.
Click the checkmark Zero Trust Mode icon.
See image.
The Zero Trust Mode menu appears. From the menu, you can:

Click the icons of your pinned browser extensions to use them during the isolation session. To use supported browser extensions (e.g., Okta Browser Plugin, 1Password) in isolation, you must have this setting enabled in your isolation profile. To learn more, see Creating Isolation Profiles for Private Access.
Click the Extensions icon to view and use supported browser extensions enabled for your isolation profile. To learn more, see Using Browser Extensions in Isolation.
Click the Protected Storage icon to view all file transfers for the isolation session. To learn more, see Transferring and Viewing Files in Isolation.

Click the Clipboard icon to use clipboard functions (e.g., copy and paste) and view notifications about restrictions configured for your isolation profile. To learn more, see Using Clipboard in Isolation.

Click the Translate icon to translate the entire web page or selected text from the web page into your preferred language. To learn more, see Understanding Language Translate for Isolation. To translate text into your preferred language, you must have this setting enabled in your isolation profile. To learn more, see Creating Isolation Profiles for Internet & SaaS and Creating Isolation Profiles for Private Access.
Click the Print icon to view options and information for printing settings. To learn more, see Transferring and Viewing Files in Isolation.
Click the More icon to view additional menu options, if available for your isolation profile.
Click the Find icon to search and find information within the web page.
Click the Troubleshoot icon to do the following:
Log out.
Start a debug session. To learn more, see Using Debug Mode for Isolation.
View network latency and export isolation session logs. To learn more, see Accessing Network Latency in Isolation.
Access ip.zscaler.com.

Click the Information icon to view the settings configured by your admin for your isolation profile. This includes restrictions and disabled tools. To view a list of your specific restrictions and disabled tools, click Restricted Actions. To learn more about possible restrictions and disabled tools, see the Security controls in Creating Isolation Profiles for Internet & SaaS and Creating Isolation Profiles for Private Access.
See image.
Click the checkmark Zero Trust Mode icon to collapse the menu options.
